content: Thomas E. Hyde, BA, DC, DABCSP, FICC, was born in 1945 in Thomasville, Georgia, to Ida and Earle Hyde. He earned his Bachelor of Arts degree in Biology from Florida State University in 1973 and later obtained his Doctor of Chiropractic degree from Logan College of Chiropractic in 1977. Following his graduation, he practiced chiropractic medicine in Miami, Florida, from 1977 to 1997. He is married to Susan Hyde and has one daughter, Jennifer. Dr. Hyde is recognized for his significant contributions to sports chiropractic, including serving as Secretary-General of the International Federation of Sports Chiropractic (FICS) and as a team doctor for the United States Olympic Committee during the 1987 Pan American Games in Indianapolis, Indiana. Beyond his professional achievements, he has also summited Mount Kilimanjaro and Mount Aconcagua, among other personal accomplishments. Dr. Hyde held the position of President and Executive Director of the American Chiropractic Association (ACA) Sports Council for eight years. He also served as Secretary-General for the International Federation of Sports Chiropractic (FICS) and acted as a liaison between FICS and the World Olympians Association. In 1987, he became the first Doctor of Chiropractic to be selected for the United States Olympic Training Center in Colorado Springs, Colorado, as part of the volunteer chiropractor program. That same year, he was chosen to represent the United States as the team doctor at the Pan American Games in Indianapolis, Indiana. In 1990, Dr. Hyde was appointed as the State of Florida's coordinator for medical services for the Sunshine Games. From 1990 to 1997, he served as the chiropractic consultant for the Miami Dolphins. In 1997, he was appointed to a four-year term on the Pan American Games and Olympic Task Force for the state of Florida. Additionally, he served on the Governor's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports. In 2001, Dr. Hyde was inducted into the ACA Sports Council Hall of Fame. In 2004, he contributed to the development of The Mercy Guidelines, a landmark set of national professional guidelines for chiropractic practice. In 2006, he became a member of the Board of Directors for the Miami-Dade Sports Commission. In 2009, he was named Person of the Year by Dynamic Chiropractic. Dr. Hyde has delivered lectures extensively across the globe, including in the United States, Canada, Hong Kong, Japan, Mexico, Argentina, Denmark, England, France, Switzerland, Australia, Chile, Brazil, Wales, and South Africa.
